hard_logic.content: From (4), X does not work night. Since Y does not work morning (1), Y must work either afternoon or night. Z cannot work afternoon (3), so Z works either morning or night. If X worked morning, Z would have to work night (2), but then Y would have to work afternoon, which is consistent. However, if X worked afternoon, Z would have to work morning, and Y would have to work night, which contradicts (4). Therefore, X works morning, Z works night, and Y works afternoon. Answer: X: morning, Y: afternoon, Z: night.
